fastimageframes.midnightconfig.title: Fast ImageFrames Settings
Packs map textures into a few big textures so all maps are drawn in one call. Biggest FPS gain on map walls.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.atlasSize: Bigger pages hold more maps per draw call (4096 = 1024 maps, 64 MB of video memory per page).
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.batchFram: Draws every item frame model in one call instead of one call per frame. No visual change.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.optimized: Only draws the faces of map frames that can be seen: walls of maps stay seamless and cost almost nothing.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.skipRedun: Vanilla rebuilds a map texture for every map packet, even when only markers moved. Only rebuild when colors change.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdLod.too: Draws the HD images of ImageFrame Client at the resolution their size on screen needs: far maps go to the map atlas, near maps keep their detail. Saves video memory and draw calls. Disabled = ImageFrame Client draws them at full resolution.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdLodQual: Texture pixels kept per screen pixel. Balanced = no visible loss. Uses your screen resolution and FOV (zoom mods included).
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdLodMinR: Far maps never go below this resolution. Only 128 lets far HD maps use the map atlas. Native = always full resolution.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdTexture: Maximum video memory for HD map textures (the atlas is not counted). Maps that are not on screen are unloaded first.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdUnloadU: Frees the video memory of HD maps that have not been on screen for this long.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdCacheSe: §lImageFrame Client HD Images: Download and Cache
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdRamCach: Compressed HD images kept in RAM, so maps can change resolution or be shown again without downloading them again.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdDiskCac: Saves the HD images of each server on disk (fastimageframes/cache) to show them instantly the next time you join.
Least recently used images are deleted beyond this size.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdTrustVa: Skip Download When Cache Is Valid
When the map shown by the server matches exactly the cached image, use it without downloading it again. Disable to always check with the server.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.hdMaxConc: HD images are requested in the order the maps appear, at most this many at the same time.
fastimageframes.midnightconfig.bakeFrame: Map frames that do not change are drawn like terrain: prepared once, then redrawn as a whole instead of one entity at a time. Frames are checked again 5 times per second. Off with hitboxes (F3+B).
fastimageframes.config.title: Fast ImageFrames
fastimageframes.config.resetPage.tooltip: Puts back the default values of this page. Nothing is saved until you press Apply or Done.
fastimageframes.config.resetAll.tooltip: Puts back the default values of every setting. Nothing is saved until you press Apply or Done.
fastimageframes.config.page.render.title: Fast ImageFrames - Map Frame Rendering
fastimageframes.config.page.render.toolt: How item frames holding maps are drawn: atlas, frame model, baked walls. These settings make map walls cheap to draw.
fastimageframes.config.page.lod.title: Fast ImageFrames - HD Images: Quality (LOD)
fastimageframes.config.page.lod.tooltip: Resolution of the HD images of ImageFrame Client depending on how far they are: presets or your own distance, video memory.
fastimageframes.config.page.cache.title: Fast ImageFrames - HD Images: Download and Cache
fastimageframes.config.page.cache.toolti: How the HD images of ImageFrame Client are downloaded and kept in RAM and on disk, so they show instantly the next time.
fastimageframes.config.enabled.tooltip: Switch for everything about item frames and maps. Off: maps and item frames are drawn exactly like vanilla, and ImageFrame Client draws its HD images itself again. Handy to compare the FPS.
fastimageframes.config.mapAtlas.tooltip: Copies the 128x128 textures of all maps into a few big pages, so a whole wall of maps is drawn with one call per page instead of one call per map. The biggest FPS gain on map walls. Needed by the baked walls, and by far HD maps.
fastimageframes.config.atlasSize.tooltip: Size of each atlas page. Bigger pages hold more maps per draw call but take more video memory: 2048 = 256 maps (16 MB), 4096 = 1024 maps (64 MB), 8192 = 4096 maps (256 MB). 4096 suits almost everyone.
fastimageframes.config.batchFrames.toolt: Draws the wooden models of all item frames together, in one call instead of one call per frame. No visual change. From Minecraft 1.21.9 the game already does it.
fastimageframes.config.optimizedFrameMod: Only draws the faces of a map frame that can really be seen: in the middle of a wall of maps, a frame costs almost nothing and the wall stays seamless. Resource packs that change the frame model (invisible frames...) are respected.
fastimageframes.config.skipRedundantMapU: The game rebuilds and uploads the texture of a map every time the server sends the map, even when only a marker moved. With this, the texture is only rebuilt when the colors really changed.
fastimageframes.config.bakeFrames.toolti: Map frames that don't change are prepared once, like terrain, then drawn as a whole instead of one entity at a time: the biggest gain on big walls. Item frames and glow item frames are both baked. Each frame is checked 5 times per second and prepared again when it changed; a change of light (torch, dynamic lights) is applied without preparing it again. Animated images (GIFs), frames with the Glowing effect outline and named frames you look at are drawn the normal way. Off with hitboxes (F3+B). Needs the map atlas.
fastimageframes.config.hdLod.tooltip: Draws the HD images of ImageFrame Client at the resolution their size on screen needs: far maps go into the atlas at 128x128, close ones keep their detail (256, 512... up to the size of the image). Saves a lot of video memory and FPS. Off: ImageFrame Client draws every image at full resolution.
fastimageframes.config.hdLodQuality.tool: How long HD maps stay sharp when you move away. Performance: lowers the resolution early. Balanced: no visible loss. Quality / Ultra: extra detail for screenshots or zoom. Custom: your own distance and delay. On your screen, maps drop to 128x128 at about %s blocks.
fastimageframes.config.hdLodCustomDistan: Distance at which an HD map is shown at 128x128, like a normal map, and moves into the atlas. Closer, its resolution doubles each time the distance is halved (256 at half this distance, 512 at a quarter...). Higher = sharper from farther, but more video memory. Zoom mods still raise the quality. Only with the Custom preset.
fastimageframes.config.hdLodCustomDowngr: How long a map must stay farther before its resolution goes down, so turning around or walking back and forth does not reload the images. The resolution goes up right away when you come closer. Only with the Custom preset (5 s with the others).
fastimageframes.config.hdLodMinResolutio: HD maps never go below this resolution, however far they are. Only 128x128 lets far HD maps use the atlas, which gives the best FPS. Native: always the full resolution of the image, the LOD then saves nothing.
fastimageframes.config.hdTextureMemoryMB: Maximum video memory used by the textures of HD maps (the atlas is not counted). Beyond it, the maps that are not on screen are unloaded first, the ones not seen for the longest time first.
fastimageframes.config.hdUnloadUnusedAft: Frees the video memory of an HD map that has not been on screen for this long. When it comes back, it is decoded again from the cache (RAM or disk), without being downloaded.
fastimageframes.config.hdRamCacheMB.tool: Compressed HD images (png) kept in RAM, to change their resolution or show them again without reading the disk or downloading them. When it is full, the images also saved on disk are dropped first, then the ones not seen for the longest time.
fastimageframes.config.hdDiskCache.toolt: Saves the HD images of each server on disk (fastimageframes/cache folder), to show them right away the next time you join, without downloading them.
Maximum size of the disk cache, all servers together. Beyond it, the images used the least recently are deleted.
fastimageframes.config.hdTrustValidatedD: Skip Download When Cache Is Valid

Each cached image is saved with the colors of its vanilla map. When the map sent by the server has exactly the same colors, the cached image is used without asking the server. Off: the server is always asked again, the cached image is only shown while waiting.
fastimageframes.config.hdMaxConcurrentRe: How many HD images are asked to the server at the same time. They are asked in the order the maps appear on screen. Higher loads a big wall faster, but asks more of the server at once.
fastimageframes.config.bakeItemFrames.to: Item frames holding other items than maps (and empty frames) are baked like map walls: recorded once with their item and replayed as a whole. Items whose look changes over time (compasses, clocks...) are noticed and drawn the normal way. Needs Baked Map Walls. Minecraft 1.21.4 to 1.21.11. No visual change.
Frames hidden behind solid blocks (walls, floors, hills) are not drawn at all, baked or not. Only opaque full blocks between you and the frame hide it, so nothing visible ever disappears. Off in the shadow pass of shader packs and for frames with the Glowing effect.
